_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED ("DO NOT EDIT") files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present and fails CI if a reprint dropped one. Provenance: issue #88 (reporter @AndrewITLive), fixed 2026-06-15 on press 4.24.0; issues #136 queries-* composite-key + object-cursor (reporter @Xenith-B), fixed 2026-06-17; issue #179 stable object-cursor offset (reporter @Xenith-B), fixed 2026-07-07.

handfixes.summary: Sync loop fetches all pages for NinjaOne after-id (keyset) endpoints. NinjaOne list endpoints (/v2/devices, /v2/organizations, ...) return a bare JSON array and paginate via ?after=<lastEntityId> - no body cursor, no envelope has_more. The generated loop only handled envelope-cursor / page / offset paginators, so it stopped at the first full page and reported a truncated dataset (e.g. 1000 of 1115 devices) as complete. --max-pages 0 had no effect because the loop broke on !hasMore before the cap mattered.
handfixes.why: determinePaginationDefaults() hard-codes cursorParam/cursorType "cursor", and extractPageItems() returns hasMore=false for a bare array (sync.go), so the natural-end break (`if !hasMore || len(items) < pageSize.limit`) fired after page 1. The press's pagination profiler does not model after-id/keyset cursors; a plain reprint regenerates the same defaults (the 0.1.1 4.24.0 regen produced byte-identical code, confirming this). The fix adds a response-shape-driven after-id fallback: when a bare-array page is full and the last item exposes an id, advance under ?after=<lastId>. Object-enveloped responses (/v2/queries/* carry a `cursor` object) are unaffected. Applied to BOTH the flat syncResource loop and the syncDependentResource loop.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: DURABLE FIX belongs in cli-printing-press: teach the pagination profiler to detect after-id/keyset pagination (bare-array list + ?after param + id-derived cursor) and emit it natively. File via printing-press-retro. Until the press learns it, this hand-fix must survive every reprint.

handfixes.summary: The device-scoped /v2/queries/* report family stored wrong/zero rows because the generic key path mis-keyed it. Two sub-symptoms: (a) the id-less reports (queries-antivirus-status, queries-device-health, queries-network-interfaces, queries-logged-on-users, queries-policy-overrides, queries-raid-controllers, queries-raid-drives) returned objects with NO top-level id -> ExtractResourceID returned "" -> every row skipped (all_items_failed_id_extraction, zero stored); (b) a broader set (queries-os-patches, queries-os-patch-installs, queries-software-patches, queries-software-patch-installs, queries-software, queries-operating-systems, queries-computer-systems, queries-processors, queries-volumes, queries-windows-services, queries-antivirus-threats) fell to genericIDFieldFallbacks and keyed on a PATCH id or a name WITHOUT a deviceId prefix, collapsing rows ACROSS devices (every 'Windows 11' device -> one stored row). Fix forces deviceId as the PRIMARY key for the whole family via resourceIDFieldOverrides, plus a per-row discriminator (productName/threatId/interfaceIndex/userName/controllerIndex/driveId/patch id/name) via the resourceCompositeKeyColumns map consulted by resourceStorageID for multi-row-per-device resources; single-row reports (operating-systems, computer-systems, device-health, policy-overrides) key on deviceId alone. The four queries-custom-fields* variants are now keyed too (#137): the source OpenAPI schema confirmed their shapes - custom-fields/custom-fields-detailed (NodeAttributes/NodeAttributesDetailed) are one row per device keyed on deviceId alone; scoped-custom-fields/scoped-custom-fields-detailed (ScopedAttributes/ScopedAttributesDetailed) are one row per (scope, entityId) keyed on entityId plus a `scope` discriminator (entityId is unique only WITHIN a scope, so a device #5 and an org #5 would otherwise collide). All four stored ZERO rows before the fix (id-less), so the overrides can only add rows.
handfixes.why: The press id profiler derives resourceIDFieldOverrides from the spec's x-resource-id / response-schema id field. NinjaOne's /v2/queries/* schemas either declare no id (so the generic fallback id/name/slug missed entirely) or declare an `id` that is a per-patch identifier shared across devices (so the fallback keyed on it and collapsed cross-device). A plain reprint regenerates the same gap. Every key/discriminator is grounded in the connector's own internal/types/types.go structs (DeviceOSPatch.id, DeviceSoftwarePatch.id, DeviceAntivirusThreat.threatId, DeviceProcessor.name, DeviceVolume.name, DeviceWindowsService.name, DeviceOperatingSystem/DeviceComputerSystem single-row, plus the #136 reporter's confirmed live shapes), never from the issue's suggested-fix text. resourceStorageID was refactored to append the resourceCompositeKeyColumns discriminator in addition to the existing resourceParentKeyColumns parent value; existing dependent-resource behavior is byte-equivalent (appends only when the field is present and non-empty). deviceId always leads the key so cross-device collapse is structurally impossible.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: DURABLE FIX belongs in cli-printing-press: teach the id profiler to detect device-scoped report endpoints and emit a composite key (scope id + a per-row discriminator) rather than keying on a non-unique id/name. File via printing-press-retro alongside the after-id/keyset profiler gap. Until the press learns it, this hand-fix must survive every reprint. Known bounded residual (deviceId always leads, so NO cross-device loss): for queries-software/queries-processors/queries-volumes the single within-device discriminator (name) can collide on rare duplicate-name rows (dual-socket identical CPUs, dup-named software variants, blank-named volumes); a multi-field composite would tighten this if a report arrives. queries-software's row shape (assumed DeviceApplication) is the one discriminator not confirmed by a typed struct. The four queries-custom-fields* variants are now keyed too (#137), grounded in the source OpenAPI schemas (NodeAttributes.deviceId; ScopedAttributes.scope+entityId), not the issue text. One bounded residual: NodeAttributesDetailed.deviceId is marked writeOnly in the spec, so if the live response omits it the override is a no-op and queries-custom-fields-detailed stays at the zero rows it already stored (never a regression); a captured live /v2/queries/custom-fields-detailed response would confirm it definitively. Second bounded residual (same class as the name-discriminator note above): the scoped variants rely on a populated `scope` to disambiguate entityId across scopes - resourceStorageID appends the discriminator only when non-empty (the shared #136 conditional-append shape), so an empty/absent scope would collapse same-id entities; this is contract-dependent (scope is the report's always-set grouping dimension) and still strictly more than today's zero rows, not a regression.

handfixes.summary: NinjaOne /v2/queries/* endpoints paginate via an OBJECT-valued cursor: "cursor":{"name":"<token>","offset":0,"count":"N","expires":...}. findCursorInMap only unmarshalled a string cursor, so the next-page token was never found; sync stopped after the first page and capped each queries resource at 100 rows (sync_warning pagination_cursor_missing). Fix adds cursorTokenFromObject, consulted by findCursorInMap only after the string unmarshal fails, which descends into the object and returns the first non-empty string token field (name/next_cursor/...). Issue #179 showed live tenants can keep cursor.name stable while cursor.offset advances; paginationProgress now compares an offset-qualified progress key and requires the same token's numeric offset to advance monotonically, so the sticky-cursor guard does not abort a progressing object cursor at 200 rows and still stops repeated or regressed offsets.
handfixes.why: determinePaginationDefaults() emits cursorParam/cursorType "cursor" but the press models a string cursor only; it does not model an object cursor whose token is nested under a field. The natural-end (len<limit), sticky-cursor, and empty-page guards already in the loop make object-cursor advance terminate safely. String-cursor APIs are unaffected because the object descent runs only after the scalar unmarshal fails. A plain reprint regenerates the string-only findCursorInMap. The #179 extension keeps sending the API's valid cursor.name token but compares cursor.name plus cursor.offset internally, so a repeated session token with advancing offset is treated as progress while repeated or regressed offsets still trip the loop-safety guard.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: DURABLE FIX belongs in cli-printing-press: teach the pagination profiler to detect object-valued cursors (cursor field is an object; token nested under name/next/cursor) and emit the descent natively, including object-cursor progress keys that can use offset when the API keeps the token stable. File via printing-press-retro. Until then this hand-fix must survive every reprint. Verification residual: multi-page completeness assumes NinjaOne advances server-side when the same cursor.name token is sent again; if a live tenant ever shows repeated rows with advancing offset, the fix must also send an offset query parameter, but the current OpenAPI surface only declares cursor plus pageSize for these report endpoints. This is monotonic vs main regardless (the sticky-cursor + max-pages guards still prevent any hang).

handfixes.summary: The MCP code-orchestration executor substitutes string path parameters from the params object, so endpoints such as custom-fields.get-node-attribute-signed-urls and tag.set-for-asset do not send literal {entityType} or {assetType} URL tokens.
handfixes.why: The generated command files call replacePathParam for string path flags, but the MCP code-orchestration path rebuilds requests from endpoint metadata. It only substituted ep.Positional placeholders before routing remaining params into the query string or JSON body. Numeric IDs worked because they were positional (for example entityId or assetId), while string path params such as entityType and assetType were left in params and the URL template stayed unresolved. The fix applies path params from positional metadata, template bindings, and any remaining params whose names still match placeholders before query/body routing.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: DURABLE FIX belongs in cli-printing-press: teach the code-orchestration executor template to consume any params matching unresolved path placeholders before query/body routing, or emit complete path binding metadata for all path params. Until then this hand-fix must survive every reprint.

handfixes.summary: doctor, the CLI error path and the MCP error path all point at `ninjaone-cli auth login` instead of a nonexistent `auth setup` subcommand (issue #277, #278)
handfixes.why: This CLI's `auth` parent defines login, status, set-token and logout. It has never defined `setup`, yet three generated surfaces told operators to run it: doctor.go's auth_hint (fires when cfg.AuthHeader() is empty), helpers.go's HTTP 400/401/403 remediation, and internal/mcp/tools.go's tool-error text -- 7 occurrences in all. Cobra does not error on an unknown subcommand of a NON-root parent (legacyArgs only rejects unknown args for the root), and the generated parent runs parentNoSubcommandRunE, which returns cmd.Help() -- a nil error. So `ninjaone-cli auth setup` printed help and exited 0. There was no 'unknown command' error and no non-zero exit anywhere in the journey: an operator saw a success code and was no closer to credentials, and because these are agent-first CLIs with typed exit codes, an agent performing setup read exit 0 as success and carried on unauthenticated. The hint fires exactly when it matters -- fresh install, rotated secret, new machine, expired token. This skill emits no auth_instructions field, so these hints are the only setup guidance it gives. The replacements name the real command and, in doctor, the variables `auth login` actually reads: NINJAONE_CLIENT_ID and NINJAONE_CLIENT_SECRET (plus the optional NINJAONE_OAUTH_SCOPE), taken from the login command's own env fallbacks rather than composed. Reported by @geekbrownbear, who verified halopsa and ninjaone live against an empty config (PR #277) and filed appdirect/crowdstrike as issue #278; the fleet scan that found the other two surfaces and confirmed only these four connectors are affected was done during triage. GENERATOR-class defect: until the press is fixed, a reprint reintroduces all 7 strings and these asserts guard them. Bug-fix-only: no new flag, command, or output field.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: DONE UPSTREAM: mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#4315 closed as completed 2026-08-25 ('already fixed on current main': the oauth2 auth hint names `auth login` since PR #2875, merged 2026-06-08, first shipped press v4.25.0); this hand-fix stays active until a reprint absorbs it, and the helpers.go and MCP tool-error surfaces must be re-checked at that reprint because upstream's closure named only doctor's auth_hint and the usage error; do NOT cite #4315 as open. Encoded there: Derive the auth hint from the subcommand set the connector actually generates instead of the fixed "Run '<cli> auth setup' for credential setup steps." string in internal/generator/generator.go. 52 of 56 connectors do define `auth setup`, which is why the hard-coded string went unnoticed; the four OAuth client-credentials connectors that scaffold `auth login` instead (appdirect, crowdstrike, halopsa, ninjaone) each shipped it 7 times. The same string is emitted into three surfaces -- doctor.go's auth_hint, helpers.go's 400/401/403 remediation, and the MCP server's tool-error text -- so a generator fix must cover all three.

asserts.contains: Set NINJAONE_CLIENT_ID and NINJAONE_CLIENT_SECRET (plus NINJAONE_OAUTH_SCOPE if your instance needs a scope), then run 'ninjaone-cli auth login' to mint a token.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

asserts.contains: report["credentials"] = "ERROR not verified: no credential is configured, so nothing was probed."
report["api"] = "not configured (base_url is a placeholder); set " + doctorBaseURLEnv + " to your own instance URL"

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For ninjaone the manifest gained: NINJAONE_BASE_URL, NINJAONE_TOKEN_URL. server.json gained: NINJAONE_BASE_URL, NINJAONE_TOKEN_URL. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: NINJAONE_BASE_URL, NINJAONE_TOKEN_URL. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: NINJAONE_NO_CONFIG_WRITE makes every credential write a no-op (token cache included) while leaving the `auth logout` erase working, and the MCP server honours it too (issue #270)
handfixes.why: Issue #270, raised by @Xenith-B off the back of #266. #266 stopped env-supplied client credentials reaching disk; the MINTED access token still landed in ~/.config/<tool>-cli/config.toml in cleartext and there was no supported way to turn that off. Their workaround was `--config NUL`, which is OS-specific, undocumented, makes doctor report a false 'not configured', and - the part that matters most - does not cover the MCP servers at all, because internal/mcp resolved its own hardcoded config path and ignored --config. Three deliberate boundaries make this switch honest rather than merely quiet. (1) ClearTokens keeps calling save() directly: it is the ERASE path, and routing it through the guard would make `auth logout` silently inert, which is a worse defect than the one being fixed. (2) `auth login` and `auth set-token` REFUSE and name the variable rather than reporting a save that did not happen - a false success is the same defect class as a doctor that says credentials are fine without checking. (3) newMCPClient now resolves through config.Load(""), the resolver the CLI uses, so the MCP server honours both NINJAONE_CONFIG and this switch; that is the half the issue says is uncovered today. The variable is declared on all three install channels because for a Claude Desktop install the manifest prompt is the ONLY channel that can set an environment variable. Class C, new documented surface. GENERATOR-class: a reprint drops the switch entirely and silently restores the plaintext token cache.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit <PREFIX>_NO_CONFIG_WRITE (or an equivalent) as part of the standard config surface, with the same three boundaries: the erase path exempt, explicit save commands failing loudly rather than no-oping, and the MCP server resolving its config through config.Load("") instead of a hardcoded home-relative path. The hardcoded path in internal/mcp/tools.go is a generator defect in its own right - it makes --config and <PREFIX>_CONFIG inert for every MCP install on every connector.

asserts.contains: | `auth login` / `auth set-token` | Refuse, naming the variable, instead of reporting a save that did not happen. |

handfixes.summary: MCP discovery exposes executor-facing request schemas and indexes input names and known enum values
handfixes.why: Issue #351: endpoint summaries omitted required request inputs. Keep canonical JSON body case and nesting, path/header/query routing, and exact short request search terms. Contracts are derived from the shipped CLI source, and the existing CLI commands and auth remain intact. Upstream request metadata fix #4890 was not merged when this surgical repair was made.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Replace this downstream contract extraction only when a released Printing Press generates equally complete executor-facing schemas and preserves every existing hand-fix.

handfixes.summary: The generator's hidden Cobra alias `create` is removed from the 10 commands listed in `why` whose POST deletes, cancels, disables, stops, rolls back or otherwise destroys or disrupts something, so `<parent> create` no longer runs them
handfixes.why: cli-printing-press gives a POST endpoint command the hidden alias `create`. On these commands the POST is destructive, so an agent that guessed the conventional verb (`<group> create`) ran the destructive call, and the alias appeared nowhere in help, agent-context or governance.md. Reproduced on origin/main 6416a241b against a local fake server: `maxio-cli subscriptions purge-json create sub_123 --ack 1` sent POST /subscriptions/sub_123/purge.json, `sentinelone-cli reports create` sent POST /reports/delete-reports and `tactical-rmm-cli agents shutdown create agent-42` sent POST /agents/agent-42/shutdown/. Fleet gate: tools/maintainer/check_command_tree.py, which walks the real cli.RootCmd() tree (137 such commands in 28 connectors on 6416a241b, 0 after). The canonical command names are unchanged; only the alias goes. A reprint re-adds it: remove it again. TestDestructiveCommandsDoNotAnswerToCreate fails while the alias is present. Commands here: alert reset alert-set-activity-data (POST /v2/alert/{uid}/reset); checklist archive-template (POST /v2/checklist/archive); device patch submit-ospatch-apply (POST /v2/device/{id}/patch/os/apply); device reboot devices (POST /v2/device/{id}/reboot/{mode}); device script run-on-device (POST /v2/device/{id}/script/run); device windows-service control (POST /v2/device/{id}/windows-service/{serviceId}/control); devices node-approval-operation (POST /v2/devices/approval/{mode}); document-templates archive document-template (POST /v2/document-templates/{documentTemplateId}/archive); knowledgebase archive-knowledge-base-articles (POST /v2/knowledgebase/articles/archive); organization archive-checklists (POST /v2/organization/archive).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: emit the `create` alias only for operations that create something.

handfixes.summary: --dry-run never mints a token or changes stored credentials: neither the client's automatic client-credentials mint nor `auth login --dry-run` sends the client secret to the token URL, and `auth set-token --dry-run` and `auth logout --dry-run` neither save nor clear anything
handfixes.why: tools/maintainer/class_harness.py write-safety found every --dry-run of a write command putting one request on the wire: authHeader ran before the dry-run branch and, with no cached token, POSTed the client ID and secret to the token URL and cached the token, while the generated comment and the docs say a dry run sends nothing. `auth login` minted through its own path and ignored --dry-run, and `auth set-token` and `auth logout` saved and cleared credentials under --dry-run (found by Codex review round 1). Same fix shape as connectwise-rmm, sophos-central and watchguard (dry-run-never-mints). TestDryRunNeverMintsAToken, TestAuthLoginDryRunSendsNothing and TestAuthSetTokenAndLogoutHonorDryRun count requests to a stub token server (each with a live control that proves the probe reaches the mint) and fail on the generated code.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press fix: client.go.tmpl should skip the client-credentials mint when DryRun is set (the dry-run preview already uses cached material only), and auth.go.tmpl's login should honor the root --dry-run flag.

asserts.contains: (dry run - no request sent, nothing saved)

handfixes.summary: Every token request (auth login, the automatic client-credentials mint and the refresh grant) goes through cliutil.OAuthTokenHTTPClient, which follows same-origin redirects only, so the client secret never reaches a host a redirect from the token URL names
handfixes.why: Owner decision on PR #441 (finish the auth-wire class). `auth login` (through http.DefaultClient) and the automatic client-credentials mint and refresh grant (through c.HTTPClient, whose CheckRedirect follows a 307 to another host) replayed the token request body, the client secret included, to whatever host a redirect from the token URL named. Printed before press 4.33.5, which routes every token request through cliutil.OAuthTokenHTTPClient (a token client that follows same-origin hops only); this back-ports that file verbatim and uses it at the same call sites. TestAuthLoginRefusesATokenRedirectToAnotherOrigin and TestTokenMintRefusesARedirectToAnotherOrigin failed on the previous commit (the second host received the token request) and pass now. The host compare is also hardened (see the newer-print entries): an IP literal compares exactly, IPv6 zone included; a DNS name folds ASCII case only.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: auth.go.tmpl and client.go.tmpl in press 4.33.5 already route token requests through cliutil.OAuthTokenHTTPClient; oauthTokenSameOrigin should compare IP literals exactly (zone included) and fold ASCII case only for DNS names.

handfixes.summary: One decoded output funnel for every server text the client shows: maskCredentialText (every API error, transport error, displayed URL and --dry-run parameter goes through it) still masks each held credential as written and URL-escaped, then withholds the WHOLE text if any held value survives in any view reachable by undoing control/format characters, JSON and JavaScript escapes, percent escapes at any depth, HTML entities, markup tags, and base64/base64url/hex runs at every alignment (cliutil.FunnelWithhold, shared byte-identical across the fleet). The held set is every value the masks cover plus the part after a scheme word and both halves of a base64 id:secret pair (Basic auth, composed keys). Surfaces funnelled here: the API error body (checked whole before the 4096-byte display cut, then again as shown); the OAuth client-credentials token endpoint's error body; the token refresh endpoint's error body. The `auth login` token exchange (internal/cli/auth.go mintClientCredentialsToken) funnels its error body with the client secret it sent. Round 3 (owner-approved structural pass): the decoder searches every view breadth-first over one fixed set of steps (control-character drop, JSON and JavaScript escapes, the identity escape as its own step, percent, HTML entities, tag strip, base64 at four alignments, hex at two), matches every view, the original included, before any filter, keeps every view a step makes (a literal backslash survives), deduplicates, and is capped by total work (512 times the input plus 4 MiB; text over 1 MiB or past the cap is withheld). Every value a funnel call is given is held process-wide (cliutil.FunnelHold), and the client holds its credentials when built and its resolved auth header on every request. Two error-only backstops withhold any held value: every command error before Cobra prints it plus every JSON/agent error envelope (internal/cli/secret_funnel_cli.go), and every MCP error result and handler error through the outermost tool middleware (cmd/<mcp>/secret_funnel_mcp.go). Success output is never funnelled.
handfixes.why: class_harness.py secret-echo (Step 3.1, PR #436) drives the built CLI and MCP server against a fake server that reflects each configured credential in every encoding; on origin/main this connector printed the credential HTML-entity-encoded, JSON-escaped, double URL-encoded or base64 (the generated masks cover only the raw, QueryEscape and PathEscape forms; press issue #5145). Matching encoded needles one at a time never converged (saas-alerts and cisco-meraki review loops), so the fix is a decode-then-check backstop that withholds the whole text and fails closed (text over 4 MiB, a decoding chain that does not settle in 32 rounds, or work past the budget is withheld). Classification is kept: the plain withheld notice avoids every word the auth-error classifiers match, and a withheld text that itself read as an auth failure gets a notice that says so (an HTTP 400 'invalid token' answer echoing the token keeps its auth exit code). Codex round 1 (2026-10-23) added that, the fail-closed depth bound (a text-like layer left at depth 8 withholds), the JavaScript escapes \v, \0 and the identity escape, a bounded \u{ search, and the token-endpoint error bodies outside the client. Known limits: values under 8 characters are only masked as written; case-changed, split-and-interleaved or otherwise transformed (compressed, encrypted) echoes are not reconstructed. A reprint that drops these edits fails class_harness.py secret-echo in CI and these asserts.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: cli-printing-press issue #5145 (encoded credential echo). The generated maskCredentialText should end in a decode-then-check backstop over every held credential, and the error-body and token-endpoint paths should check the whole body before the display cut.

asserts.contains: func (c *Client) shownSummary(body []byte, summary string, extraCredentials ...string) string {

handfixes.summary: Every reader follows NinjaOne's two paging shapes to the end, not only sync: bare-array lists keyed by the last item id (?after=) and /v2/queries/* reports with an object cursor. extractResourcePage wraps the rendered reader with the keyset and short-page rules (shared leaf package internal/ninjapage); the object cursor's offset rides in the internal cursor and only the token is sent; paged exports skip the response cache; the MCP bound pager takes its page size from the request and computes the keyset next cursor; MCP report pages read the object cursor.
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.0 stops a full bare-array page as incomplete but never advances, so export devices stopped at page one and reported done, export queries and MCP report pages read the object cursor as absent, and MCP bare-array pages reported count = page size with no next_cursor.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Teach the press keyset (after-id) and object-cursor pagination; until then this survives every reprint.

handfixes.summary: An MCP continuation cursor for a report keeps the page it was issued for, scoped to the path and query, so a repeated call never replays NinjaOne's stateful report cursor into a different walk.
handfixes.why: A replayed report cursor returned the wrong page to an agent.

handfixes.summary: The client-credentials token request resolves its scopes as a list (default control management monitoring, or NINJAONE_OAUTH_SCOPE split on whitespace) and joins them at form.Set("scope"); the request on the wire is unchanged.
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.0 dogfood's OAuth scope check reads only this shape and failed every endpoint on the rendered single literal.

handfixes.summary: Root help reads NinjaOne CLI and auth help reads Manage authentication for NinjaOne (the press renders Ninjaone).
handfixes.why: cli-printing-press#5226: the press title-cases the slug.

handfixes.summary: The token mint in auth.go and client.go returns its raw error to hand wrappers (ninja_token_errors.go) that funnel the token endpoint's error body with the client ID and secret it sent before any caller sees it.
handfixes.why: A token endpoint error body that echoed the client ID or secret reached callers that do not hold it.

handfixes.summary: A local or auto read of an endpoint reads the partition sync stores that endpoint under, and a write only writes through to the partition it can change.
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.0 named partitions by the alphabetically first endpoint, so local reads of several endpoints read another endpoint's rows.

handfixes.why: doctor reported the default US instance as a placeholder.

handfixes.summary: Five groups' primary sync partition stays on the endpoint the shipped release stored there (queries = /v2/queries/disks, backup = jobs, organization = documents, user = roles); antivirus-status syncs under queries-antivirus-status.
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.0 re-points each group to its alphabetically first endpoint, so an upgraded store would mix two endpoints' shapes in one partition and freeze queries-antivirus-status (av-sweep and fleet-health read it).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Pin partition names in the spec (x-resource-name) for the next print.

handfixes.summary: /v2/organization/documents rows are keyed on documentId (ClientDocumentWithAttributeValuesPublicApiDTO), not organizationId.
handfixes.why: Keyed on organizationId, every document of an organization collapsed into one stored row.

handfixes.summary: sync judges a short page against the page size it actually requested (a user pageSize or limit), not the endpoint default.
handfixes.why: A requested page smaller than the default looked short and ended the walk after one page.

handfixes.summary: sync asks /v2/queries/volumes for include=bl so BitLocker status is stored for bitlocker-gaps.
handfixes.why: Without include=bl the volumes report omits bitLockerStatus and every volume read as NOT_REPORTED.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: default: bl on the /v2/queries/volumes include parameter.

handfixes.summary: Dependent resources read their parent ids from the partition the parent is actually synced under.
handfixes.why: After the partition-name pin the generated lookup read an empty partition and synced no dependents.

handfixes.summary: backup-coverage judges protection from the documented backup usage report fields.
handfixes.why: It read undocumented fields and reported protected devices as unprotected.

handfixes.summary: A /v2/queries/* report row is keyed on its documented identity. Reports whose row schema has no per-item id (disks, antivirus-status, logged-on-users, processors, software, volumes, windows-services) are keyed on device id plus the row's ordinal among that device's rows in one walk (stamped _ninja_row_ordinal, counted across pages, walked from page one). Those position-keyed rows are written only by a walk that also replaces the whole report: the walk stages its stamped pages in a 0600 file beside the store and writes nothing while it walks; a walk that is complete, from page one, with only row-preserving parameters (one classifier, ninjaReportWalkParams: pageSize as a positive integer, include on /v2/queries/volumes), no since window or tenant scope, and only report-row pages replaces the partition in ONE transaction (store.ReplaceReportRows; shipped-key rows go too). Any other walk (capped, stuck, non-JSON or single-object page) writes nothing and reports reconcile_skipped + report_not_stored; a walk that fails on a page writes nothing and returns that resource's error. A row-narrowing parameter (any other, or unknown, key; a since window) on such a report is refused before any request, as a critical per-resource failure. --no-prune does not apply to them (a whole walk replaces them and says no_prune_not_applicable); workflow archive replaces them too. Every other report keeps the replace on every complete unfiltered walk unless --no-prune, judged by the same classifier; a filtered, resumed, capped or failed walk of one deletes nothing.
handfixes.why: Two same-named processors of one device collapsed into one row, and an ordinary sync kept a software version an upgrade replaced, so software-audit reported two installs where NinjaOne reports one. Codex r1 and the 2026-10-26 adversarial review then showed that any walk that wrote position-keyed rows without replacing the whole report (a documented filter such as installedAfter or state=STOPPED, pageSize misread as a filter, --max-pages, a failed later page, --no-prune) lost a row NinjaOne still returns or stored one twice.

retired.reason: tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Press 4.34.0 keeps the environment markers through SaveTokens and generates MarkCredentialsExplicit, so a client ID or secret read from the environment is never written by a token save.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Press 4.34.0 builds a per-command blocked set (blockedDestinationFlags, blockedInputFlags, root control-plane flags), removes those flags from each tool's schema, refuses any undeclared argument name (so "db=/path" is refused) and skips '=' names in cliArgsFromMCP.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Upstreamed as cli-printing-press #4647: every value-carrying branch of cliArgsFromMCP joins the value to its flag (--k=v, one element per list item), and the press generates TestCliArgsFromMCP_ValueCannotSmuggleBlockedFlag.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: The note paused HTTP mode until a reprint because the build served HTTP with no token. Press 4.34.0 HTTP mode refuses to start without <PREFIX>_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN, answers 401 without the right bearer, binds 127.0.0.1 by default and refuses a non-loopback address without TLS; onboard.py now writes HTTP guidance that follows the binary (cc-skills #14) and never writes this note, so the entry would fail on every re-onboard.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Press 4.34.0's cobratree mirror derives one blocked set per command (destination, input, mcp:write-flags, mcp:read-flags and root control-plane flags), leaves those flags out of the tool schema and refuses them, and any undeclared argument, by name.
